paras.text: … For example, if someone sells an old house built earlier, its value should not be included in gross national product. However, the commission of the property dealer connected with its purchase and sale can certainly be included, because he has performed a new service by bringing together the seller and the buyer of the house. However, if some new house is built, its value will become part of gross national product.

paras.text: vi. National product produced abroad: gross national product is in fact the value of goods and services produced by the labour of a country’s own factors of production. Therefore this matter is worth attention, that if a resident of one country is working in another country, his income too will be counted part of gross national product. For example, many workers of Pakistan go to other countries and earn and send back to the country; therefore that earning too should be counted part of the gross national product of Pakistan. In the same way, if the industrialists of Japan set up some factory in Pakistan, they will send their profit from here back to their country, which will be the national product of Japan, and that profit will not be part of the gross national product of Pakistan.

paras.pashto: vi. په بهر کې تولید شوی ملي تولید: ناخالص ملي تولید په حقیقت کې د یوه هېواد د خپلو تولیدي عواملو په کار د تولید شویو توکو او خدمتونو ارزښت دی. نو دا خبره د پام وړ ده چې که د یوه هېواد اوسېدونکی په بل هېواد کې کار کوي، د هغه عاید به هم د ناخالص ملي تولید برخه وشمېرل شي. د بېلګې په توګه د پاکستان ډېر کارکوونکي نورو هېوادونو ته ځي، ګټه کوي او هېواد ته یې بېرته لېږي؛ نو هغه ګټه هم باید د پاکستان د ناخالص ملي تولید برخه وشمېرل شي. همداسې که د جاپان صنعتکارانو په پاکستان کې کومه فابریکه جوړه کړې وي، له دې ځایه به خپله ګټه بېرته خپل هېواد ته لېږي چې د جاپان ملي تولید به وي او هغه ګټه به د پاکستان د ناخالص ملي تولید برخه نه وي.

paras.text: 2. Sum of the remunerations of the factors (National Income at Factor Prices)
paras.urdu: 2۔ عاملین کے معاوضوں کا مجموعہ: (National Income at Factor Prices)
paras.pashto: 2. د عواملو د معاوضو مجموعه (National Income at Factor Prices)

paras.text: The second method of measuring national income is that the remunerations received by all the factors of production be added up, i.e. if the “rent” which the owners of land get, the “interest” to the owners of capital, the “wages” to labourers, and the profit which organisers obtain are added up, then national income will come.

paras.pashto: د ملي عاید د اندازه کولو دویمه طریقه دا ده چې ټولو تولیدي عواملو ته ورکړل شوې معاوضې جمع شي، یعنې د ځمکې مالکانو ته چې کوم "لګان"، د پانګې مالکانو ته "سود"، مزدورانو ته "مزدوري" او تنظیم‌ګرو ته چې کومه ګټه ترلاسه کېږي، جمع شي، نو ملي عاید راځي.

paras.text: This method too is based on the first method, in this way: when goods are produced, there are two aspects of it. One is that a particular quantity of things is produced, and the buyers pay its price. The second aspect is that the people who produce goods get remuneration in return for it. For example, in a factory one thousand yards of cloth is prepared. On one side, people will buy it and pay its price, and on the other side this price paid will be distributed as remuneration among all the people, i.e. the factors of production, who together prepared this cloth. As it were, they will obtain income. Thus on one side the price of the goods produced and on the other side the incomes of those producing the goods will both be equal. Therefore, to find national income, whether we find the value of all goods or add up the incomes of those who produce them, the result will in any case remain the same. Therefore national income can be measured by both these methods.

paras.pashto: د ملي عاید د اندازه کولو درېیمه طریقه دا ده چې په هېواد کې پر بېلابېلو توکو او خدمتونو ټول لګښت جمع شي، ځکه څومره چې شیان تولیدېږي، هغه پېرل کېږي هم. لګښت دوه ډوله وي: لومړی د مصرف کوونکو پر توکو لګښت چې مصرفي لګښت بلل کېږي، او دویم پر پانګه‌ییزو توکو لګښت چې د پانګونې لګښت بلل کېږي. نو د لګښتونو د مجموعې په طریقه د ملي عاید د اندازه کولو لپاره باید لاندې لګول شوې پیسې جمع شي.

paras.text: ii. General expenditure of the government: i.e. those sums which the government spends at the state level on buying goods of its need and on other government departments and institutions, e.g. defence, hospitals, educational institutions, roads, courts, police, media etc.

vi۔ بیرونِ ملک پیدا ہونے والی قومی پیداوار: خام قومی پیداوار درحقیقت کسی ملک کے اپنے عاملینِ پیدائش کی محنت سے پیدا کردہ اشیاء و خدمات کی مالیت ہے۔ لہٰذا یہ بات قابلِ توجہ ہے کہ اگر ایک ملک کا باشندہ کسی دوسرے ملک کام کر رہا ہو تو اس کی آمدنی بھی خام قومی پیداوار کا حصہ شمار ہوگی۔ مثلاً پاکستان کے بہت سے کارکن دوسرے ممالک میں جا کر کمائی کرتے اور واپس ملک میں بھیجتے ہیں۔ اس لئے وہ کمائی بھی پاکستان کی خام قومی پیداوار کا حصہ شمار ہونی چاہیے۔ اسی طرح اگر جاپان کے صنعت کاروں نے پاکستان میں کوئی کارخانہ لگایا ہو تو وہ یہاں سے اپنا نفع واپس اپنے وطن بھیجیں گے۔ جو جاپان کی قومی پیداوار ہوگی۔ اور وہ منافع پاکستان کی خام قومی پیداوار کا حصہ نہیں ہوگا۔

2۔ عاملین کے معاوضوں کا مجموعہ: (National Income at Factor Prices)

قومی آمدنی کو ماپنے کا دوسرا طریقہ یہ ہے کہ تمام عاملینِ پیدائش کو ملنے والے معاوضے جمع کر لئے جائیں یعنی زمین کے مالکوں کو جو ”لگان“، سرمائے کے مالکوں کو ”سود“، مزدوروں کو ”اجرتیں“ اور ناظموں کو جو منافع حاصل ہوتا ہے وہ جمع کر لیا جائے تو قومی آمدنی آئے گی۔

یہ طریقہ بھی پہلے طریقے پر ہی مبنی ہے۔ وہ اس طرح کہ جب اشیاء پیدا ہوتی ہیں۔ تو اس کے دو پہلو ہوتے ہیں: ایک یہ کہ چیزوں کی خاص مقدار پیدا کرتے ہیں۔ اور خریدنے والے اس کی قیمت ادا کرتے ہیں۔ دوسرا پہلو یہ ہے کہ جو لوگ اشیاء پیدا کرتے ہیں۔ انہیں ان کے بدلے معاوضہ ملتا ہے۔ مثال کے طور پر ایک کارخانے میں ایک ہزار گز کپڑا تیار ہوتا ہے۔ ایک طرف تو لوگ اسے خرید کر اس کی قیمت ادا کریں گے۔ اور دوسری طرف یہی ادا کردہ قیمت ان تمام لوگوں یعنی عاملینِ پیدائش میں بطور معاوضہ بانٹ دی جائے گی۔ جنہوں نے مل کر یہ کپڑا تیار کیا ہے۔ گویا انہیں آمدنی حاصل ہوگی۔ تو اس طرح ایک طرف پیدا شدہ اشیاء کی قیمت اور دوسری طرف اشیاء کو پیدا کرنے والوں کی آمدنیاں دونوں برابر ہوں گی۔ اس لیے قومی آمدنی معلوم کرنے کے لئے خواہ ہم تمام اشیاء کی مالیت معلوم کر لیں یا ان کی پیدا کرنے والوں کی آمدنیاں جمع کریں۔ نتیجہ بہر حال یکساں رہے گا۔ چنانچہ ان دونوں طریقوں سے قومی آمدنی کی پیمائش ہو سکتی ہے۔

i۔ عام لوگوں کا صرفی خرچ: یعنی تمام رقوم جو ملک کے عوام اپنی ضرورت کی اشیاء و خدمات پر خرچ کرتے ہیں۔

… For example, if someone sells an old house built earlier, its value should not be included in gross national product. However, the commission of the property dealer connected with its purchase and sale can certainly be included, because he has performed a new service by bringing together the seller and the buyer of the house. However, if some new house is built, its value will become part of gross national product.

vi. National product produced abroad: gross national product is in fact the value of goods and services produced by the labour of a country’s own factors of production. Therefore this matter is worth attention, that if a resident of one country is working in another country, his income too will be counted part of gross national product. For example, many workers of Pakistan go to other countries and earn and send back to the country; therefore that earning too should be counted part of the gross national product of Pakistan. In the same way, if the industrialists of Japan set up some factory in Pakistan, they will send their profit from here back to their country, which will be the national product of Japan, and that profit will not be part of the gross national product of Pakistan.

2. Sum of the remunerations of the factors (National Income at Factor Prices)

The second method of measuring national income is that the remunerations received by all the factors of production be added up, i.e. if the “rent” which the owners of land get, the “interest” to the owners of capital, the “wages” to labourers, and the profit which organisers obtain are added up, then national income will come.

This method too is based on the first method, in this way: when goods are produced, there are two aspects of it. One is that a particular quantity of things is produced, and the buyers pay its price. The second aspect is that the people who produce goods get remuneration in return for it. For example, in a factory one thousand yards of cloth is prepared. On one side, people will buy it and pay its price, and on the other side this price paid will be distributed as remuneration among all the people, i.e. the factors of production, who together prepared this cloth. As it were, they will obtain income. Thus on one side the price of the goods produced and on the other side the incomes of those producing the goods will both be equal. Therefore, to find national income, whether we find the value of all goods or add up the incomes of those who produce them, the result will in any case remain the same. Therefore national income can be measured by both these methods.

3. Sum of expenditures (Expenditure Method)

The third method of measuring national income is that the whole expenditure made on different goods and services in the country be added up, because whatever things are produced are also bought. Expenditure is of two kinds: first, expenditure on goods for consumers, which is called consumption expenditure; and second, expenditure on capital goods, which is called investment expenditure. Thus, to measure national income by the method of the sum of expenditures, the following sums spent should be added.

i. Consumption expenditure of the common people: i.e. all those sums which the public of the country spend on goods and services of their need.

ii. General expenditure of the government: i.e. those sums which the government spends at the state level on buying goods of its need and on other government departments and institutions, e.g. defence, hospitals, educational institutions, roads, courts, police, media etc.

iii. Gross domestic private investment: i.e. that sum which the common people spend on setting up factories within the country, on completing new projects and development schemes, or on buying new types of machines in place of old machines. It is also called replacement expenditure.

iv. Gross domestic government investment: i.e. that sum which the government spends within the country for the purpose of investment, e.g. expenses on development projects …

… projects and constructional works, the expenses incurred on them.

v. Net foreign investment: people of one country go to another country and invest, and people of outside countries come into it and invest. If people here have invested more in foreign countries while people of our country … people invested less in this country, then the difference of both, i.e. net investment, will be positive. In the reverse conditions investment will be negative; therefore this net foreign investment too should be included in production.

vi. Difference between exports and imports: if a country’s exports are equal to its imports, it means that as much sum as outside people spent here, that much the people here spent outside. But if exports are more, it means that outside people spent relatively more sum here. Therefore an amount equal to this difference too should be added to national income.

Total gross national product = private consumption expenditure + government consumption expenditure + private investment + government investment + net foreign investment + difference of imports and exports

2. Circular Flow of National Income

Every economy has two sectors: one households and the second business institutions. Thus in a two-sector economy national income can be shown through a circular flow. The mutual relationship of the two methods of measuring national income mentioned above can be shown by diagram no. 1.

In this diagram there are two parties.

First party: households

That is, common people who work in the capacity of different factors of production and receive a reward in return for it. For example, among the public some people are doctors, some engineers, organisers, artisans, labourers, clerks, traders, drivers etc. All these people go and work in business institutions in the form of factors of production, as the arrow no. 1 on the left side of the outer circle shows. In return for this work these factors of production receive their remuneration, e.g. the owner of a building takes rent and those doing business obtain profit, as the arrow no. 2 on the left side of the inner circle shows.

مجموعی خام قومی پیداوار = نجی صرفی خرچ + سرکاری صرفی خرچ + نجی سرمایہ کاری + سرکاری سرمایہ کاری + خالص غیر ملکی سرمایہ کاری + درآمدات اور برآمدات کا فرق

2۔ قومی آمدنی کا دائری بہاؤ (Circular Flow of National Income)

ہر معیشت کے دو شعبے ہوتے ہیں۔ ایک گھرانے اور دوسرا کاروباری ادارے۔ چنانچہ دو شعبہ جاتی معیشت میں قومی آمدنی ایک دائری بہاؤ کے ذریعے ظاہر کی جا سکتی ہے۔ قومی آمدنی ماپنے کے مذکورہ بالا دونوں طریقوں کے باہم تعلق کو ڈائیگرام نمبر 1 سے ظاہر کیا جا سکتا ہے۔

اس ڈایاگرام میں دو فریق ہیں۔

پہلا فریق گھرانے:

یعنی عام لوگ جو مختلف عاملینِ پیدائش کی حیثیت سے کام کرتے ہیں اور اس کے عوض صلہ پاتے ہیں۔ مثلاً عوام میں بعض لوگ ڈاکٹر ہیں بعض انجینئر، ناظم، کاریگر، مزدور، کلرک، تاجر، ڈرائیور وغیرہ یہ سب لوگ عاملینِ پیدائش کی شکل میں کاروباری اداروں میں جا کر کام کرتے ہیں۔ جیسا کہ بیرونی دائرے کے بائیں طرف کا تیر نمبر 1 ظاہر کرتا ہے۔ اس کام کے عوض یہ عاملینِ پیدائش اپنا اپنا معاوضہ وصول کرتے ہیں۔ مثلاً عمارت کے مالک کرایہ لیتے ہیں اور کاروبار کرنے والے نفع حاصل کرتے ہیں۔ جیسا کہ اندرونی دائرے کے بائیں طرف کا تیر نمبر 2 ظاہر کرتا ہے۔
